question: Among the three universities that joined the Atlantic Coast Conference in 2024, which was founded earliest?
notes: Cal 1868 < Stanford 1891 < SMU 1911; gap 23 yrs. Stanford 1885 charter date doesn't change the order.

question: Among the universities that joined the Atlantic Coast Conference in 2013, which was founded most recently?
notes: Syracuse 1870 > Notre Dame 1842 > Pitt 1787; gap 28 yrs. Notre Dame joined non-football; answer is Syracuse whether or not ND is counted.

question: Of the two universities that joined the Atlantic Coast Conference in 2004, which one is older?
notes: Virginia Tech 1872 vs Miami 1925; gap 53 yrs. Boston College joined 2005, not 2004 - common confusion, that's the trap.
aliases: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University

question: One of the Atlantic Coast Conference's founding members later left the conference to join the Big Ten. Which current ACC member was founded in the same decade as that departed school?
notes: Hard, sequential: departed charter member (Maryland, left 2014) -> its founding year (1856) -> scan 18 current members -> only FSU (1851) is in the 1850s. Nearest others: BC 1863, Duke 1838. FSU's 1857 opening date is also 1850s. Replaces uni-4 (Pitt, earliest post-2000 joiner), which was retired after probing at 3 steps / 12 parallel tool calls: wide, not hard.

question: Among the towns that border Acton, Massachusetts, which has the largest land area?
notes: Attribute: land area. Neighbors per Acton page: Westford 30.6 sq mi > Concord 24.9 > Sudbury 24.4 > Stow 17.6 > Littleton 16.6 > Carlisle 15.4 > Boxborough 10.4 > Maynard 5.2. Margin 23%.

question: Among the cities and towns that border Lexington, Massachusetts, which was incorporated most recently?
notes: Attribute: incorporation year. Belmont 1859 > Winchester 1850 > Arlington 1807 > Burlington 1799 > Lincoln 1754 > Waltham 1738 > Bedford 1729 > Woburn 1642. Margin 9 yrs; neither date contested.

question: Among the cities and towns that border Natick, Massachusetts, which has the most water area?
notes: Attribute: water area (total minus land; usually not stated directly). Framingham 1.5 sq mi > Wayland 0.7 > Wellesley 0.3 = Weston 0.3 > Sherborn 0.2 > Dover 0.1. Framingham is 2x the runner-up.

question: A Massachusetts town was once known as 'Wood End'. Of the towns bordering it, take the one with the largest land area. Among the towns bordering that town, which has the largest land area?
notes: Hard, sequential: Wood End -> Reading -> neighbors (Wilmington 17.1 > N. Reading 13.3, 22%) -> Wilmington's neighbors -> Andover 31.0 > Billerica 25.9 (18%). Shortcut check: Reading's own largest neighbor is Wilmington, so skipping the second border hop gives a wrong answer. North Andover will REVIEW, not PASS.
